items.stem: You need a reusable document design that users start from but cannot accidentally overwrite. What should you create?

options.text: A regular .docx saved as read-only once
options.rationale: A read-only document is fragile and not a template.
Correct: a template (.dotx) is designed to be the starting point for new documents and preserves the original design.
A PDF cannot be edited as a starting document.
A macro file does not supply the document design.

items.explanation: Correct: a template (.dotx) is designed to be the starting point for new documents and preserves the original design.

items.stem: Which feature generates a table of contents that updates automatically when headings change?

options.text: A manually typed list of page numbers
options.rationale: A typed list does not update automatically.

options.text: A table of contents built from heading styles
options.rationale: Correct: a TOC built from heading styles can be refreshed to reflect heading and page changes.
A text box does not track headings.
Bookmarks mark locations but do not build a TOC.

items.explanation: Correct: a TOC built from heading styles can be refreshed to reflect heading and page changes.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid uses of a Word mail merge? (Select TWO)

options.text: Producing personalized letters from a recipient list
options.rationale: Correct: mail merge personalizes letters from a data source.

options.text: Generating address labels from a data source
options.rationale: Correct: labels are a standard mail-merge output.
Mail merge does not compile macros.
Encryption is not a mail-merge function.

options.text: Converting the document to a template automatically
options.rationale: Mail merge does not create templates.

items.explanation: Both keyed options are correct; all-or-nothing scoring requires exactly the keyed set.
